title: Local finite-sum kernel models for Hom out of a coherent module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $\mathcal F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every point $x\in X$ there are an open neighbourhood $U\ni x$, integers $m,n\geq0$, and an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\alpha:(\mathcal F|_U)^{\oplus n}\to(\mathcal F|_U)^{\oplus m}$ such that $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)|_U\cong\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha)$ as $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The sums are finite categorical biproducts, including the empty sum when a rank is zero, and restrictions are along the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow X$. No coherence or Noetherian assumption is imposed on $\mathcal F$ or $X$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BW (lemma-coherent-finite-presentation); Lemma 01CQ (lemma-internal-hom-locally-kernel-direct-sum), first assertion; proof of Lemma 01CP (lemma-stalk-internal-hom).

proof.text: ($\mathcal G$ is locally finitely presented.) Let $x\in X$. Since $\mathcal G$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] there are an open $U\ni x$ and a surjection $\psi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$. By the second condition of coherence [pqf-def-coherent] the kernel $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}\psi$ (sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) is of finite type, so there are an open $V$ with $x\in V\subseteq U$ and a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal K|_V$. Since kernels are computed sectionwise, $\mathcal K|_V=\operatorname{Ker}(\psi|_V)$, and the composite $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal K|_V\subseteq\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ gives an exact sequence $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\psi|_V}\mathcal G|_V\to0$ of $\mathcal O_V$-modules. Thus $X$ is covered by opens $V$ each carrying such a presentation of $\mathcal G|_V$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BW (lemma-coherent-finite-presentation, line 1596) and its proof, cited as 'finitely presented' in Lemma 01CQ

proof.text: (Restriction to $V$.) For an open $V\subseteq X$ the restriction $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)|_V$ equals $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_V}(\mathcal G|_V,\mathcal F|_V)$ as $\mathcal O_V$-modules: by the definition of the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] both have as sections over an open $W\subseteq V$ the $\mathcal O_W$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(\mathcal G|_W,\mathcal F|_W)$, with the same restriction maps and the same module structure.

source.place: Section 04TT (sites-modules-section-internal-hom), definition of the internal Hom and its restriction to a localized site (Lemma 0E8H, lemma-internal-hom-restriction, line 3775)

proof.text: Apply the left exact precomposition sequence [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-kernel] to the finite free presentation on $U$ from step 1. Evaluation on a finite free basis identifies Hom from each free term with the finite biproduct of copies of $\mathcal F|_U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Transport the two maps along these isomorphisms. Exactness at the first two terms says that the first map is monic and identifies its source with the kernel of the next map [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Combine with the restriction identification of step 2. The same universal properties apply when either rank is zero.
